analysis.investment_thesis: Ravelcare fails the Magic Formula on both dimensions: ROE of 0.67% signals essentially zero return on capital, while a P/E of 19.2 implies an earnings yield of only ~5.2% — neither cheap nor good. A digital-first BPC micro-cap with no demonstrated capital efficiency is exactly what the Magic Formula is designed to screen out.
key_strengths: Operating in a structurally growing BPC/D2C category
Small 100 Cr cap leaves room for optionality if execution improves
key_risks: ROE of 0.67% — capital is effectively earning nothing
Earnings yield ~5.2% (P/E 19.2) is well below the 12% Magic Formula threshold
Tiny 100 Cr cap in hyper-competitive BPC vs Nykaa, HUL, Honasa
red_flags: ROE <1% — either razor-thin margins or bloated capital base
Valuation (19x P/E) disconnected from return profile
Incorporated only 2018 — no 3-year track record of sustained ROIC
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Magic Formula lens, this is an immediate reject. The two inputs I care about — Return on Capital and Earnings Yield — are both weak. ROE of 0.67% tells me capital is being severely under-utilized; even adjusting for leverage, ROIC here cannot plausibly clear my 20% bar. Meanwhile, P/E of 19.2 translates to an earnings yield of roughly 5.2%, well below the 12% I demand and nowhere near the 15%+ that would make me interested despite business-quality concerns.

Qualitatively, a 2018-incorporated D2C beauty brand at 100 Cr market cap is competing against Nykaa, Honasa/Mamaearth, and HUL — a category where customer acquisition cost eats gross margin alive. Promoter holding of 72.94% is a mild positive, but systematic investing doesn't reward narrative; it rewards numbers. Until earnings yield approaches double digits AND ROIC sustainably crosses 20% for multiple years, this stays out of the portfolio.
